label: Rich presence status
summary: A short status phrase about what the character is up to, such as "Conquering the World as".
details: It has 84 entries. The game checks them in order and uses the first one whose condition fits, with a default phrase (rich_presence_default) as the last resort. Conditions include having the barbershop screen open, conquering the world (a huge realm, or the Mongol empire title), plague traits, epidemics in the realm, wars, raiding, prison, activities, stress, schemes and dying. The two examples shown in the input end in "as" ("Tending weeping buboes as"), but only the first four texts were available, so that is not known for every entry. Going by the name, this is the status line shown on the player's online profile; the input does not say so outright.

label: Servant for romance
summary: The name of a servant job, such as a stable boy, page or scullery maid.
details: The entries are stable boy, page, scullery maid, chandler, launderer, naperer, scalder and saucerer. The game picks the one that matches the flag stored in the character's variable `servant_romance_target`. Each gives the job title in lower case, to be placed inside a sentence.

label: Sex scene text
summary: The whole text of a romance scene, built from four parts one after another.
details: Its single entry joins the opening (part 1) and the middle (part 2) into one paragraph, then adds the third part and the ending as two further paragraphs, with blank lines between. Each part is written from the character's point of view and uses the saved scope named `second` as the partner. So a `second` scope must be set when the text is shown.

label: Sex scene ending
summary: The closing paragraph of the romance scene, in one of two forms.
details: If the character has the variable `sex_scene_location`, the game uses the location-based ending; otherwise it uses the random ending. Each entry just calls another custom text of the same kind, with the saved scope `second` as the partner.

label: Ending by location
summary: An ending paragraph that fits the place of the scene: garden, private chambers, stables, copse or kitchen.
details: The place comes from the character's variable `sex_scene_location` (flags garden, private_chamber, stable, copse, kitchen). The kitchen has two endings. The last entry is the general random ending. The game marks it as valid for random choice. The texts are in the first person, and the partner is referred to as `second`.

label: Random ending
summary: A general ending paragraph that does not depend on the place.
details: It has six variants, each a few sentences in the first person about the aftermath. The partner is referred to as `second`. The game marks it as valid for random choice, so it can pick any one of them.

label: Scene opening
summary: The opening of the romance scene, in one of two forms.
details: If the character has the variable `sex_scene_location`, the game uses the location-based opening; otherwise it uses the random opening. Each entry just calls another custom text of the same kind, with the saved scope `second` as the partner.

label: Opening by location
summary: An opening that fits the place of the scene: garden, private chambers, stables, copse or kitchen.
details: The place comes from the character's variable `sex_scene_location`. The last entry is the general random opening. The texts are in the first person and name the partner as `second`; some also mention the partner's relation to the speaker and the residence building. The game marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Random opening
summary: A general opening that does not depend on the place.
details: It has eight variants in the first person. The partner is referred to as `second`, and one variant also uses the character's clothing article. The game marks it as valid for random choice.

label: Scene middle
summary: The second part of the romance scene (it follows the opening in the same paragraph), one of nine variants.
details: Each variant is a first-person passage that uses the partner as `second`. The game marks it as valid for random choice, so it can pick any one of them.

label: Scene third part
summary: The third part of the romance scene, one of six variants.
details: Each variant is a first-person passage that uses the partner as `second`. The game marks it as valid for random choice, so it can pick any one of them.

label: Signature weapon
summary: The name of a weapon: sword, mace, axe, hammer, spear or dagger.
details: The game picks the one that matches the flag stored in the character's variable `signature_weapon`. Sword is also the fallback when nothing matches. It gives the weapon word in lower case, to be placed inside a sentence.

label: Flood-covered adjective
summary: An adjective describing the character: irritable, proud, beautiful, or unsuspecting as a fallback.
details: "Irritable" needs the wrathful trait, "proud" the arrogant trait, and "beautiful" a good beauty trait (rank 1 or higher). "Unsuspecting" is used when none of those fit. The game marks it as valid for random choice, so if several fit it can pick any of them.

label: Stewardship level word
summary: A word for how good the character's stewardship skill is: terrible, poor, average, good or excellent.
details: By vanilla's script: terrible below 3, poor from 3 to 10, average from 11 to 14, good at 15, excellent at 16 or more.

label: Stewardship level (genitive)
summary: The same five stewardship levels (terrible, poor, average, good, excellent), in a genitive form.
details: It uses the same skill thresholds as the plain stewardship level text. Vanilla defines it in its Polish customizable localization file, and the entries' texts exist only in the Polish localization (the input shows none), so it is meant for a grammatical form of that language.

label: Subject of interest
summary: A topic a character might talk about, such as court politics, trade routes, poisons or hunting.
details: It has 21 entries; the game marks it as valid for random choice, so it picks one of the entries that fit. Some entries are limited by the character's education type (for example military topics for a martial education, court politics for a diplomacy education). Examples are troop compositions, tax levels, parties, friendship, lawmaking and "ancient military campaigns".

label: Surprised reaction
summary: A word for being surprised: amazed, astonished, aghast, horrified, thrilled or awed.
details: None of the entries has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for random choice, so it picks any one of the six. Some are positive and some negative.

label: Theme announcement
summary: The name of a theme: nobility or romance.
details: The game picks the one that matches the flag stored in the character's variable `poetry_theme`. It gives the theme word in lower case, to be placed inside a sentence.

label: Generous adjective
summary: A word that describes the character's attitude to giving: wasteful, magnanimous or munificent.
details: "Wasteful" is used for a character with the greedy trait, "magnanimous" for one with the generous trait, and "munificent" for everyone else.

label: Greedy adjective
summary: A word that describes the character's attitude to wealth: rapacious, acquisitive or avaricious.
details: "Rapacious" is used for a character with the generous trait, "acquisitive" for one with the greedy trait, and "avaricious" for everyone else.

label: Impatient adjective
summary: A word that describes the character's patience: unreliable, dynamic or restless.
details: "Unreliable" is used for a character with the patient trait, "dynamic" for one with the impatient trait, and "restless" for everyone else.

label: Lustful adjective
summary: A word that describes the character's attitude to desire: lecherous, playful or lascivious.
details: "Lecherous" is used for a character with the chaste trait, "playful" for one with the lustful trait, and "lascivious" for everyone else.

label: Number word
summary: A number written out in words, picked at random: seven, eleven, twelve or twenty.
details: None of the entries has a condition and the game marks it as valid for random choice. The name says "two syllable", but only seven and twenty have two syllables in English, so the name is not exact. Vanilla keeps it in its poetry word file.

label: Own title word
summary: The lower-case word for a ruler's title: emperor, empress, king, queen, duke, duchess, count, countess, baron or baroness.
details: The rank comes from the character's highest held title (empire, kingdom, duchy, county, otherwise barony). The male or female form is chosen by the sex of the saved scope `second`, not of the character, so a `second` scope must be set.

label: Vassal directive icon
summary: The small icon for the directive a vassal follows, such as improving development or training commanders.
details: The texts are icon codes in the form `@name!`, for example `@task_develop_county!`. The game picks by the character flags `vassal_directive_*`; with none of them set, the "no directive" icon is used. There is also one for refusing the directive, one for each directive type (build men-at-arms, convert faith or culture, building focus, fertility, explore cultures, raiding intent), and a blank line. Only four texts were shown in the input.

label: Vassal directive text
summary: A sentence saying what directive a vassal is following, for example "Using the ... councillor task".
details: There is one for no directive ("This vassal has no directive"), one for refusing it, and one for each directive type, plus a blank line. It is chosen from the character flags `vassal_directive_*`. Some sentences take the name from the councillor task text. Only four texts were shown in the input.

label: Vassal directive with icon
summary: The icon and the short text of a vassal's directive together, such as an icon followed by "Improve development".
details: It covers the same cases as the icon and the text versions: no directive ("None"), refusing, and every directive type, plus a blank line. Only four texts were shown in the input.

label: Virtue choice
summary: The name of a virtue, such as brave, just, temperate, chaste or generous.
details: It has 19 entries. The game picks the one that matches the flag in the saved scope `virtue_choice`, not the character's own traits, so that scope must be set. The entries include gentle and harsh words (forgiving, wrathful, vengeful, greedy, lustful, gluttonous), so they are not all good traits. Only four texts were shown in the input.

label: Weak claim requirement
summary: Describes who counts as too weak to hold a claim: "incapable or a child", plus "or a woman" or "or a man" in some cases.
details: The women-weak text is used when the game parameter `female_claims_are_weak` applies, and the men-weak text when `male_claims_are_weak` applies. The general text is used when `tenet_hyperdulia_female_claims_are_strong` applies and as the last fallback. The checks run in that order. The general entry is listed twice because it appears both first and last.

label: Wealth
summary: A word for the character's wealth: "Rich" or "Poor".
details: "Rich" is used when the character has more than 50 gold. With less than 50 gold, one of four poor entries is chosen at random. At exactly 50 gold no entry fits. The input shows no text for the last three poor entries.

label: Wet or hard
summary: One of the words "wet" or "hard", chosen by the character's sex.
details: "Wet" is used for a female character and "hard" for a male one. Vanilla keeps it in the file of the romance scene texts.
